answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with the value of transactions it handles, reaching a summit only after sustained honest work. New identities start with tiny limits, so creating thousands of fake agents costs far more in locked capital than any single fraud can earn, while a glacier-slow reputation thaw means a caught cheater cannot simply reappear under a new name and regain trust instantly. A juniper root system offers the right image: many visible shoots, one costly shared root of verified history.
